reviews.review:
This game is perfect the first 2 hours that you play it. It looks good, plays well, and seems to promise a lot of unlocks and replayability in the future. If this was an early access game, I'd recommend it. Sadly, it's not. And the more you play, the more you realize that your anticipation for things to come is just your optimism. And the things you get the first 2 hours is it. It's unfinished otherwise.

There's only 1 biome and you get about 15 levels until the boss fight. Pretty short. First time I rolled credits, I thought maybe it unlocked something new. It didn't. Maybe it's like Hades and you get more unlocks the more you beat it? After 5 more times of rolling credits and getting exactly the same dialog and being unceremoniously dumped back to the hub area with nothing new, it's apparent that that's really just it.

The game brags "Experiment with thousands upon thousands of builds". Technically true, but doesn't work in practice. You get 4 spell slots with up to 5 modifiers (some spells have less). Remember the 1 biome, 15 levels? The run is so short that forget the other slots, you can barely even fill in all the modifiers for your starter spell even if you always go for upgrade doors. A thousand builds might be possible, but not probable. You always get the same starter spell and the same handful of modifiers to choose from before the run ends abruptly.

Hub area gives you Leto (the globe for upgrades), 2 NPCs, 2 tomes, an empty spot, a large door, and the lift to the levels. So when you play the first few hours, you're expecting more things from the hub. You're excitedly thinking: this is gonna be good as I unlock things. Nope. One NPC gives you a weak attempt at world building, the other one eventually gives you a trinket. That's it. The 2 tomes, the empty spot, and large door? Nothing. Just decorations. What you get the first time you start the game is the same hub you get after rolling credits multiple times.

If you're looking for something to play for a few hours, beat once, and not play again. You can consider this. But if you're looking for a game with a long tail, different strategies, multiple biomes, plenty of replayability, this ain't it. Maybe that was the original intent, and they made a great start. But they decided to release it as just that: a great start, but obviously unfinished.
